reasoning: Lodged corn plants with prominent purple/reddish-bronze discoloration on stalk internodes and fully dried tan-brown leaves. The purple stalk rind discoloration combined with whole-plant lodging is the hallmark presentation of Anthracnose stalk rot (Colletotrichum graminicola), which causes characteristic shiny black to purple-bronze discoloration of the lower stalk rind with internal rotting and eventual lodging.
